title: Iff-split of the sequential characterization of continuity into forward and metric converse
intent: Prove the sequential characterization of continuity (continuous iff it maps convergent sequences to convergent sequences, the converse under metrizability) by splitting it into its forward implication and its metric converse, each stated and proved as its own named lemma, and gluing them as the two `shows` clauses of Theorem_21_3.
also_known_as: iff on a characterization with a side condition

parent.name: Theorem_21_3
parent.statement:
theorem Theorem_21_3:
  assumes hTX: "is_topology_on X TX"
  assumes hTY: "is_topology_on Y TY"
  assumes hmap: "\<forall>x\<in>X. f x \<in> Y"
  shows "top1_continuous_map_on X TX Y TY f
          \<longrightarrow> (\<forall>s x. seq_converges_to_on s x X TX
                 \<longrightarrow> seq_converges_to_on (\<lambda>n. f (s n)) (f x) Y TY)"
    and "top1_metrizable_on X TX
          \<longrightarrow> (\<forall>s x. seq_converges_to_on s x X TX
                 \<longrightarrow> seq_converges_to_on (\<lambda>n. f (s n)) (f x) Y TY)
          \<longrightarrow> top1_continuous_map_on X TX Y TY f"

children.name: Theorem_21_3_forward
children.statement:
theorem Theorem_21_3_forward:
  assumes hTX: "is_topology_on X TX"
  assumes hTY: "is_topology_on Y TY"
  assumes hcont: "top1_continuous_map_on X TX Y TY f"
  assumes hx: "seq_converges_to_on s x X TX"
  shows "seq_converges_to_on (\<lambda>n. f (s n)) (f x) Y TY"
children.closed_by: structured proof that unfolds seq_converges_to_on_def, top1_continuous_map_on_def and neighborhood_of_def and closes each conjunct from the local hypotheses by blast/simp; no project lemma is cited
children.note: Self-contained leaf: the proof is definition-unfolding plus automation on the hypotheses, so a bounded prover can close it on its own.

children.name: Theorem_21_3_converse_metric
children.statement:
theorem Theorem_21_3_converse_metric:
  assumes hd: "top1_metric_on X d"
  assumes hTY: "is_topology_on Y TY"
  assumes hmap: "\<forall>x\<in>X. f x \<in> Y"
  assumes hseq:
    "\<forall>s x. seq_converges_to_on s x X (top1_metric_topology_on X d)
          \<longrightarrow> seq_converges_to_on (\<lambda>n. f (s n)) (f x) Y TY"
  shows "top1_continuous_map_on X (top1_metric_topology_on X d) Y TY f"
children.closed_by: top1_metric_topology_on_is_topology_on, then the closure criterion Theorem_18_1(1), with Lemma_21_2_sequence and Lemma_21_2_sequence_converse establishing the closure inclusion
children.note: Closes from named project lemmas only: it does not re-prove the sequence lemmas, it wires them to the closure criterion.

applicability.goal_shape: A characterization P iff Q, or the two implications P ⟶ Q and (side condition ⟶ Q ⟶ P), where the two directions need different arguments; here continuous ⟺ sequential, with the converse conditional on top1_metrizable_on X TX.
applicability.use_when: the two directions have different proofs (forward is definitional — a continuous preimage of a neighbourhood; converse needs the metric sequence lemma), so each deserves its own named lemma; and one direction carries an extra hypothesis (metrizability) used only by that direction.
applicability.avoid_when: a single argument proves both directions (then state one lemma); the directions share so much that a plain iffI/intro with no intermediate lemmas is clearer; or the side condition must be threaded through the whole theorem instead of being isolated in one child.

consequences: Splitting a characterization into two named lemmas obliges the glue to state each `shows` clause exactly matching a lemma's conclusion, and to feed each lemma the hypotheses it lists (hTX, hTY, hcont, hx for the forward; hd, hTY, hmap, hseq' for the converse). The converse direction forces the metrizability hypothesis into its own child, so the glue must first unfold top1_metrizable_on_def to obtain a metric d, then re-wrap the sequential hypothesis over the metric topology (hseq') before applying the converse lemma. Failure mode: if the side condition is not isolated in its own child, the unconditional forward direction would also carry it, weakening the theorem.
